appraisal_events.evidence: « Voulez-vous vous taire, petit sot, répondit-il avec colère, et ne pas avoir l'air grotesque de considérer comme peu de chose l'honneur d'être probablement... reçu par moi. »
appraisal_events.explanation: Charlus angrily scolds the narrator as a 'little fool' for seeming to undervalue the honor of being received by him, staging the narrator as chastised and subordinate in the exchange.

status_effects.explanation: The narrator is repeatedly rebuked and mocked by Charlus within the staged conversation (called 'petit sot', told he doesn't know who Whistler is, met with 'le ton le plus méprisant'), losing composure and standing relative to Charlus in this direct exchange.

ambiguities: The passage ends mid-dialogue with an unanswered question comparing the princesse de Guermantes to the duchesse de Guermantes ('La princesse de Guermantes est supérieure à la Mme de Guermantes ?'); no completed evaluative event regarding duchesse de Guermantes occurs within this excerpt.

The phrase 'entre tous les Courvoisier et Gallardon' reads as a generic reference to families/types of the faubourg Saint-Germain milieu rather than a specific evaluative event targeting the individual character marquise de Gallardon, so it was not scored as an event against her.
The mention of the princesse de Parme is purely genealogical (identifying her as mother of the duc de Guastalla) with no direct evaluative content, so she was not scored.
